newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - ICA earnings seen poor.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ICA earnings seen poor.

text.p: Mexican construction firm Empresas ICA is expected to post poor fourth quarter and 1996 revenues and earnings, but the figures have already been discounted by the market, analysts said.
A Reuters survey of six equity analysts forecast average net 1996 earnings of 3.86 pesos per share, compared with 7.19 pesos per share in 1995.
Analysts said non-cash items and those relating to toll- road concessions run by the company would distort net earnings.

Lower building activity and tighter margins will weaken ICA's earnings, partly as a result of the company completing its laying of a cable network for telephone company Avantel during the third quarter.

"The top line will come in low now that the Avantel project is over. The comparison against the fourth quarter of '95 will also be weak," said Christopher Hussey, an analyst with Goldman Sachs in New York.
Ben Uglow, of Flemings Research, agreed.
"ICA will not post strong operating figures, but the market already knows that and I would say it is discounted in the share price," he said.

Gerardo Saenz, of the OBSA-GSerfin brokerage, estimated ICA's 1996 sales at 7.603 billion pesos, or 3.7 percent below 1995 figures in real terms. Operating earnings would fall by 15.4 percent year-on-year, however, to 457 million pesos, resulting in an operating margin of six percent, compared with 7.4 percent in 1995.
